_comment: Manifest read by the genji-sync skill. It lives here, in the template, so it is versioned alongside the code it describes: the skill always reads the copy at the target ref.

merge.package.json: Take dependencies, devDependencies, the pnpm block (overrides, onlyBuiltDependencies) and packageManager. Keep the project's own name, version, description, and any scripts it added or changed. Never copy the template's version over the project's. templateVersion is the project's record of which template release it is on: the template has no such field, so never delete it — set it to the target version at the end of the sync.
merge.next.config.ts: Union, never replace. Take new or changed security headers, but keep every origin the project added to connect-src / img-src / frame-src — its RPC, API and CDN hosts are not the template's business. A project on a different chain will have a different RPC in connect-src; that entry must survive. If the project has no headers() block or no CSP at all, it lost them in a refactor rather than choosing to drop them: restore this file's whole security block, then add the project's own origins to connect-src. A missing CSP only shows up in production, so check for its presence on every sync, not just for changed directives.
merge..env.template: Add new variables, keep the project's own.
merge.src/context/index.tsx: Provider composition. Add providers the template introduced, keep providers the project added.
merge.src/app/layout.tsx: Take structural changes, keep project-specific metadata, fonts and analytics.
merge.src/translations/index.ts: Project-owned branding text — never delete or overwrite a key the project already has. But add every key and locale genji introduces that the project is missing, so the project's UI never falls back to an undefined string. Keys that only serve a page in the never list are the exception — about.* and navigation.about belong to src/app/about, which customize.js deletes, so a project without that page does not need them and adding them is dead weight. If a new key needs project-specific wording (a product name, a URL), add it with genji's default text and flag it in the sync report for the user to localize.

_neverNote: src/app/about, src/app/api, docs/, CHANGELOG.md and customize.js are removed by customize.js when a project is created. Re-adding them would undo that. pnpm-lock.yaml is never copied — it is regenerated by pnpm install. .genji-version is legacy: projects generated before templateVersion moved into package.json still have it, and genji-sync migrates them, so it must never be copied from the template either. src/components/Header.tsx is never synced as a file — its chrome (logo, links, colors) is project-branded — but the login/logout button it renders (or that a project extracted into its own component) should still be checked for behavioral parity with genji's: the hasLocalCredentials()/isNoPasskeyError auth flow, and the registration dialog's fields, copy and alreadyRegisteredLink. Only the branding differences are the project's to keep; the auth mechanics and copy are not.
